scenes.title: Cloud Compute Basics (EC2 & VMs)
scenes.narration: A virtual machine like an EC2 instance is a rented computer in the cloud where you run your code, databases, and data processing jobs.

scenes.title: What a VM Gives You
bullets: A full operating system you control, so you can install any software your pipeline needs.
A choice of instance types that balance CPU, memory, and storage for your workload.
The ability to start, stop, and resize on demand so you only pay while it runs.
scenes.narration: A virtual machine hands you a complete operating system where you have full control to install whatever you need. Instance families let you pick the right mix of CPU, memory, and disk for the job. Because you can stop instances when idle, you avoid paying for compute you are not using.

scenes.title: Launching an Instance
steps: Pick an instance type and size
scenes.narration: Starting a VM follows a predictable sequence. You select a machine image that defines the operating system, choose an instance type sized to your workload, and attach storage plus a network configuration. After launch you connect over SSH to begin working.

scenes.title: On-Demand vs. Spot Instances
scenes.narration: On-demand instances cost a fixed rate and run until you stop them, which suits steady or critical workloads. Spot instances offer huge discounts by using spare capacity, but the provider can reclaim them at short notice. For interruptible batch data jobs, spot pricing can slash costs dramatically.

scenes.title: Managing an EC2 Instance
scenes.code:
# Launch an instance from an AMI
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0abcd1234 \
  --instance-type t3.large --key-name my-key

# Stop it when idle to save money
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids i-0123456789
scenes.narration: The CLI lets you script instance management instead of clicking through the console. The run-instances command launches a VM from a chosen image and type, while stop-instances halts it. Automating the stop step is one of the easiest ways to cut a surprising amount of wasted spend.

scenes.text: A cloud VM is just a computer you rent by the hour — right-size it, stop it when idle, and use spot pricing for interruptible jobs to keep costs sane.
scenes.narration: Think of a VM as a rentable computer billed by time. Right-sizing it, stopping it when idle, and reaching for spot instances on tolerant workloads together keep your compute bill under control.
